record.original_question: Characterize all connected signed graphs whose adjacency spectrum consists of exactly two distinct eigenvalues.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.9 (Signed graphs with exactly 2 distinct eigenvalues). Characterize all connected signed graphs whose spectrum consists of two distinct eigenvalues.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a finite simple graph and $\sigma\colon E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a signature on its edges. Its adjacency matrix $A^\sigma$ is the symmetric $|V|\times|V|$ matrix with entries $A^\sigma_{uv}=\sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise. The spectrum of $(G,\sigma)$ is the multiset of eigenvalues of $A^\sigma$. The signed graph is connected if its underlying graph $G$ is connected.

Problem: Give a complete characterization of all connected signed graphs $(G,\sigma)$ whose adjacency spectrum consists of exactly two distinct eigenvalues. That is, classify, up to switching equivalence and isomorphism, all such pairs $(G,\sigma)$ for which $A^\sigma$ has only two distinct eigenvalues.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization remains open. Partial classifications are known: any such signed graph must be regular; complete classifications exist for small maximum degree (degree at most 4, and degree 5), for small numbers of vertices (e.g., 12 and 13 vertices), and for triangle-free regular cases via a balance condition on positive/negative paths of length two between non-adjacent vertices. Related work has also addressed two main eigenvalues and cospectrality questions.
